# Dephasing Control Geometry

> Research account of optimal eigenstate transfer under fixed commuting Hermitian dephasing and bounded Hamiltonian spectral width, with explicit gate constructions and coherent-workspace resource bounds.

## Entry point

- [README](README.md): main result, science and learning routes, resource boundaries, reproduction command and purpose.

## Routes by reader intention

- Physical story: [learning introduction](learning/README.md), then [interpretation](science/interpretation.md). The three-level example explains why a longer route can reduce basis error while increasing phase error.
- Study: [30-milestone map](learning/MILESTONES.md), supported by the [Breuer–Petruccione bridge](learning/BREUER_PETRUCCIONE_BRIDGE.md). The map has 14 background/preliminaries milestones and 16 narrative/innovation milestones. It is common to all readers.
- Theorem and proof: [model](science/model.md), [geometry](science/geometry.md), [finite-noise proof](science/finite_noise.md), then the relevant construction or workspace result.
- Reproduction: [verification guide](verification/README.md), its documented command and the stored analytic expectations.
- Attribution: [related work](references/RELATED_WORK.md), then the linked primary sources and their stated access limits.

## Single educational anchor

Heinz-Peter Breuer and Francesco Petruccione, The Theory of Open Quantum Systems, Oxford University Press, 2007 paperback, ISBN 9780199213900. The [source bridge](learning/BREUER_PETRUCCIONE_BRIDGE.md) owns the verified chapter mapping, convention translations and locally supplied steps. Primary research citations are retained for attribution and proof dependencies; they do not add educational anchors.

## Authoritative scientific statements

- [Model](science/model.md): use this file for the exact dissipator normalization, error definition, control budget and theorem quantifiers.
- [Geometry](science/geometry.md): shortest-path certificate, inherited binary crossing kernel, matching upper bound and special spectra.
- [Finite-noise proof](science/finite_noise.md): converse for the actual mixed trajectory, valid for every finite duration and noise-dependent protocol.
- [Constructions](science/constructions.md): phase-free selective pulses, exact success products, endpoint X and controlled X, logical Choi weights and full-channel budget.
- [Control resources](science/control_resources.md): distinguish global spectral halfwidth from operator norm or per-term amplitude; state selective-access assumptions and charge dimension and duration.
- [Workspace](science/workspace.md): local label-mixing budgets, joint return error, workspace entropy and a finite coherent repetition circuit.
- [Interpretation](science/interpretation.md): physical examples and limits of spectral refinement.

## Evidence and reproduction

- [Related work](references/RELATED_WORK.md): precise attribution, nearest comparisons and source-access limits.
- [Bibliography](references/references.bib): primary source identifiers.
- [Verification guide](verification/README.md): deterministic finite-dimensional checks and their limits.
- [Verification runner](verification/run_all.py): executable comparison with stored analytic expectations.
- [Expected values](verification/expected_results.json): analytic reference values and tolerances.

## Interpretation constraints

- The squared noise-distance representation and the two-level scalar optimum are established prior results. Attribute them as specified in Related work.
- The exact equality is the leading weak-noise optimum for a fixed finite model. The displayed finite-noise rational expression is a lower bound.
- The noise graph is a complete graph of costs, not automatically a hardware coupling graph. Restricted connectivity does not inherit an exact shortest-path optimality claim.
- Population error includes leakage. Logical Choi weights are unconditioned. Single-logical-qubit Pauli coefficients are not the coefficients of the controlled gate.
- Fixed-span spectral refinement and increasing an unnormalized noise spectrum are different comparisons. Refinement charges helper levels, control access, duration and phase error.
- The growing phase-error expression is a fixed-dimension first-order coefficient. The fixed-noise, growing-ladder coherence statement has its own nonperturbative estimate in Constructions.
- Joint pure-work return and data-only accuracy after retaining or discarding syndromes are different tasks. The workspace result is not a universal data-only error floor or an erasure-heat theorem.
- The workspace entropy asymptotic requires data error e=o(R) as R tends to zero. Keep that condition with any entropy-order claim.
- Numerical examples check formulas and conventions; they do not establish arbitrary-control optimality or exhaustive priority.
